questions.question: A sum of Rs. x is divided among A, B and C such that the ratio of the shares of A and B is 3 : 4 and the ratio of the shares of A and C is 5 : 8. If the difference between the shares of B and that of C is Rs. 312, then the value of x will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the shares of A and B is 3 : 4

The ratio of the shares of A and C is 5 : 8. 

The difference between the shares of B and that of C is Rs. 312

**Concept used:**

Concept of ratio and proportion

**Calculation:**

Let A and B be 3 y and 4 y

So, A: B = 3 y: 4 y × 5 ----(1)

And A: C = 5 y: 8 y × 3 -----(2)

From (1) and (2)

A = 15 y

B = 20 y

C = 24 y

According to the question,

24 y - 20 y = 312

⇒ 4 y = 312

⇒ y = 78

Now, we have to find the value of x = A + B + C

⇒ 15 y + 20 y + 24 y

⇒ 59 y

⇒ 59 × 78

⇒ 4602

**∴ The value of x will be Rs 4602.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**A : B = 3 : 4

A : C = 5 : 8

To Make A equal put in the ratio A : B : C 

A : B = (3 : 4)5 = 15 : 20

A : C = (5 : 8)3 = 15 : 24

A : B : C = 15 : 20 : 24

B - C = 312

24u - 20u = 312

4u = 312

1u = 78

A + B + C = 15u + 20u + 24u = 59u

59 × 78 = 4602 Rs

questions.question: A shopkeeper blends two varieties of tea, one costing Rs. 320 per kg and another costing Rs. 240 per kg, in the ratio 9 : 11. If he sells the mixture at Rs. 325.68 per kg, then his gain percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two varieties of tea, one costing Rs. 320 per kg and another costing Rs. 240 per kg.

He sells the mixture at Rs. 325.68 per kg

Average CP of mixed tea when mixed in ratio 9:11

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP - CP

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

Average CP of mixed tea when mixed in ratio 9:11

⇒ (320×9 + 240×11)over(9+11) = (2,880+2,640)over20 

CP = 5520over20 = Rs. 276

SP = Rs. 325.68

Profit = 325.68 - 276 = Rs. 49.68

Gain % = 49.68over276 × 100 = 18%

**∴ The gain percentage is 18%.**

questions.question: Pipes A and B can empty a tank in 15 hours and 18 hours, respectively. Pipe C alone can fill the tank in 6 hours. If all the three pipes are opened together, then two-third part of the tank will be full after:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of tank = LCM(15, 18, 6) = 90 units.

Efficiencies: Pipe A = −6, Pipe B = −5, Pipe C = +15 (Net efficiency = 15 − 11 = +4 units/hr).

Target work = 2/3 of total capacity = (2/3) × 90 = 60 units.

Time required = Target work ÷ Net efficiency = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to empty = 15 hours

Time taken by Pipe B to empty = 18 hours

Time taken by Pipe C to fill = 6 hours

**Calculation:**

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency (Units/Hr)**
 
 

 A (Empty)
 15
 90
 −6
 
 

 B (Empty)
 18
 −5
 
 

 C (Fill)
 6
 +15
 
 

⇒ Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = (−6) + (−5) + 15

⇒ Net efficiency = 15 − 11 = 4 units/hr (Positive sign implies the tank is filling)

⇒ Target part of the tank to be filled = 2/3 of 90 units

⇒ Target work = (2 ÷ 3) × 90 = 60 units

⇒ Time required = Target work ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Time required = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sign Convention for Pipes

Always assign a positive efficiency to an inlet (filling) pipe and a negative efficiency to an outlet (emptying) pipe or a leak.

Combined Rate of Filling

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, then their net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x − 1/y). If the result is positive, the tank fills; if negative, the tank empties.

Concept of Fractional Work

Time required to complete a specific fraction of a tank = (Fraction × Total Capacity) ÷ Combined Efficiency.

questions.question: The cost price of two articles A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4. While selling these articles, the shopkeeper gains profit of 10% on article A and 20% on article B and the difference in the selling price is Rs. 560. The sum of the cost prices of article A and B (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of CP of articles A and B is 5 : 4

Profit on article A = 10%

Profit on article B = 20%

The difference in the selling price is Rs. 560

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100

**Calculation:**

Let CP of articles A and B be 50x and 40x respectively

Then SP of article A = 50x × (100 + 10)/100 = 55x

SP of article A = 55x

And SP of article B = 40x × (100 + 20)/100 = 48x

SP of article B = 48x

According to the question,

⇒ 55x - 48x = 560

⇒ 7x = 560

x = 80

Now, the sum of CP of both articles = 50x + 40x = 90x

⇒ 90x = 90 × 80 = 7200

**∴ The sum of the cost prices of article A and B is 7200.**

**NOTE:- As CP's are in the ratio 5 : 4. So by taking CP's 50x and 40x calculation becomes easier.**

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 4,900 in 3 years 4 months at the rate of 7.5% p.a. at simple interest. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum in 3{3{} over 4} years at the rate of 8% p.a. simple interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest in 1st case = 7.5% × (10/3) = 25% → Amount = 125% of Principal.

Effective interest in 2nd case = 8% × (15/4) = 30% → Amount = 130% of Principal.

Since 125% of Principal = ₹4900

130% of Principal = (4900 ÷ 125) × 130 = 39.2 × 130 = ₹5096.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5096.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount in 1st case (A₁) = ₹4900

Rate (R₁) = 7.5% p.a., Time (T₁) = 3 years 4 months = 3 + 1/3 = 10/3 years

Rate (R₂) = 8% p.a., Time (T₂) = 3 + 3/4 = 15/4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI = P × (1 + RT/100)

 
 Sum (P)

 

 

 
 A₁ = 4900
 7.5% for 10/3 yr
 SI = +25%

 

 

 
 A₂ = 5096
 8% for 15/4 yr
 SI = +30%

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the 1st case, SI₁% = 7.5 × (10/3) = 25%

⇒ Amount (A₁) = 100% + 25% = 125% of P

⇒ 125% of P = ₹4900

⇒ P = (4900 × 100) ÷ 125 = ₹3920

⇒ In the 2nd case, SI₂% = 8 × (15/4) = 30%

⇒ Amount (A₂) = 100% + 30% = 130% of P

⇒ A₂ = 130% of 3920 = (130 ÷ 100) × 3920

⇒ A₂ = 1.3 × 3920 = ₹5096

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5096.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate in SI

In Simple Interest, the effective interest percentage for a given period is simply the product of the rate and time (R × T)%. This allows for direct calculation without finding the principal every time.

Amount Formula for Simple Interest

Amount (A) = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100). The principal remains constant throughout the entire period, unlike compound interest where interest is added to the principal.

Simple vs Compound Interest

For the first year, both simple and compound interests are identical (if compounded annually). From the second year onwards, CI will be greater than SI because interest is earned on accumulated interest.

questions.question: A person deposited Rs. 8,000 in a term deposit for 1 and a half year, which gives half yearly compounded interest at a rate of 10% per annum. The compound interest will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Deposited amount = 8000

TIme = one and half year = 18 months or 3 half year

Rate of interest = 10% per annum

Interest is compounded half yearly

Rate of interest for 6 month = 5%

**Concept:**

Amount (A) = P (1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

Amount = 8000 × (1 + 5/100)³

= 8000 × (21/20)³

= 8000 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20

= 21 × 21 × 21 

= 9261

The compound interest = 9261 - 8000 = 1261

∴ Compound interest will be 1261

questions.question: The average height of 35 students in a group is 156 cm. If 8 students of average height 154.5 cm leave the group and 13 students of average height 158 cm join the group, then what will be the average height (in cm) of all the students now in the group?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average height of 35 students in a group is 156 cm.

8 students of average height 154.5 cm leave the group

13 students of average height 158 cm join the group

**Calculation:**

Average height of 35 students in a group is 156 cm.

Total height of 35 students = 35 × 156 = 5460 cm

8 student who leave the group total height = 8 × 154.5 = 1236 cm

Total height of 27 student = 5460 - 1236 = 4224 cm

Now, who joined in the group newly total height of newly admitted 13 students = 13 × 158 = 2054 cm

Now, total 40 students total height = 4224 + 2054 = 6278 cm 

Average of 40 student height = 6278/40 = 156.95 cm 

∴ The average height of 40 students is 156.95 cm

questions.question: A train travels at a speed of 108 km/h and another train at a speed of 25 m/sec. The ratio of speed of first train to that of the second train is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the first train = 108 km/h

Speed of the second train = 25 m/sec

Speed in km/h = (Speed in m/sec) × (18/5)

**Calculation:**

questions.question: Honey and Junnu together can finish a certain work in 20 days. Honey having worked for 12 days, Junnu finished the remaining work alone in 36 days. In how many days can Junnu finish the whole work alone?
questions.solution:

Honey and Junnu together can finish a certain work in 20 days.

Honey having worked for 12 days, and

Junnu finished the remaining work alone in 36 days.

Work = Efficiency × Time

According to the question,

⇒ 12 H + 36 J = 20 × (H + J)

⇒ 12 H + 36 J = 20 H + 20 J

⇒ 16 J = 8 H

⇒ J/H = 1/2 (Efficiency ratio)

Total work = Efficiency × time

⇒ 20 × (1 + 2)

⇒ 60

Junnu finish the whole work alone in = 60/1

⇒ 60 days

**∴ The Required days are 60.

questions.question: Two trains running in opposite direction on parallel tracks, at the speed of 48 km/h and 52 km/h, take 27 seconds to cross each other. If the lenght of one train is 350 m then find the length ( in metres) of the other train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 48 + 52 = 100 km/h = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s.

Total distance (Sum of lengths) = Speed × Time = (250/9) × 27 = 750 m.

Length of the other train = Total distance − First train length = 750 − 350 = 400 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the first train (S₁) = 48 km/h

Speed of the second train (S₂) = 52 km/h

Time taken to cross each other (T) = 27 seconds

Length of the first train (L₁) = 350 m

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Total Distance (L₁ + L₂) = Relative Speed × Time

 
 Train 1 : 48 km/h
 Length = 350 m
 
 
• 
 

 

 
 Train 2 : 52 km/h
 Length = ?
 
 
• 
 

 

 27 sec
 

 

 
 Relative Speed = 48 + 52 = 100 km/h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 48 + 52 = 100 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Total Distance = (250/9) × 27

⇒ Total Distance = 250 × 3 = 750 m

⇒ L₁ + L₂ = 750

⇒ 350 + L₂ = 750

⇒ L₂ = 750 − 350 = 400 m

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds. Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Stationary Object

When a train crosses a stationary pole or man, the total distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train.

Crossing a Bridge or Platform

When a train crosses a stationary bridge or platform, the total distance covered is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the bridge/platform.
